thesis: Ciena is the only large pure-play optical networking vendor and AI has made its gear scarce: fiscal Q3 2026 revenue grew 37% to a record $1.67B, adjusted operating margin hit a record 22.5%, adjusted EPS tripled to $2.11, and backlog jumped $800M to $8.5B with management guiding above $10B by fiscal year-end. FY2027 revenue is guided to at least $8.3-8.4B (described as a supply-constrained floor) with 25-27% adjusted operating margin, and the FY2029 framework targets a ~30% revenue CAGR, ~50% gross margin and ~20% FCF margin. Yet the stock sits ~46% below its June 2026 high of $637.51 on a sector-wide AI-optics de-rating, leaving a 30%+ grower at roughly 29x estimated FY2027 adjusted EPS. Primary risk is hyperscaler concentration - two customers were 41.7% of Q3 revenue - and the AI capex cycle behind that demand.

drivers: Component supply unlocks faster than the FY2028 rebalancing management assumes, lifting FY2027 well above the $8.3-8.4B floor
WaveLogic 6 Extreme holds its 1.6T lead and pulls attached line-system revenue with it
RLS Hyper-Rail standardizes by end of calendar 2026 and ramps to several hundred million dollars in FY2027 at step-function-better economics
Coherent optics move inside the data center at 3.2T, expanding TAM beyond DCI into intra-facility links
FY2029 framework delivers: ~30% revenue CAGR to roughly $14B, ~50% adjusted gross margin, 32-35% operating margin, ~20% FCF margin

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands at the guided $6.42B and FY2027 delivers close to the $8.3-8.4B floor, producing estimated adjusted EPS of $11-12 (own calculation from guided revenue and 25-27% operating margin, ~20% tax, ~148M diluted shares). Adjusted gross margin normalises to 45-46% as the one-time tariff refund rolls off, pricing gains hold through FY2027, and the multiple stays near 35-40x forward earnings - closing most of the gap to the ~$493 sell-side consensus without needing the FY2029 targets fully de-risked.

risks: Hyperscaler optical orders digest in FY2027-28 and the $10B backlog is re-read as pull-forward rather than genuine lead-time demand
Customer concentration bites: two customers were 41.7% of Q3 revenue and DCOM revenue is explicitly lumpy
Supply normalisation in FY2028 reverses the high-single-digit to low-20s percent price increases customers accepted under scarcity
Multiple compresses from ~29x toward 18-20x on flat-to-lower earnings, retracing toward the $143.19 52-week low and the $185 low sell-side target
Canadian tariff regime costs ~$10M per quarter and working capital funding of long-term supply agreements suppresses free cash flow

catalysts.event: Q4 and FY2026 results plus formal FY2027 guidance — confirms the $6.42B FY2026 landing, whether FY2027 is guided above the $8.3-8.4B floor, and whether backlog prints above $10B
RLS Hyper-Rail standardization — gates the several-hundred-million-dollar FY2027 ramp
FY2026 Form 10-K — updated customer concentration and long-term supply agreement disclosure
Q1 FY2027 results — first read on whether price increases and Hyper-Rail economics hold
Component supply capacity additions under the supply agreements locked through 2029 — the main source of upside to the guided floor

key_risks: Customer concentration: two customers each above 10% of revenue, 41.7% combined in Q3 FY2026
AI capex cyclicality — management claims a ~two-year buffer from connecting existing data centers and GPU refresh, not immunity
Supply constraints cap revenue: the FY2027 guide is a floor set by component availability, and funding supply agreements consumes working capital
Margin sustainability: ~70 bps of the 46.4% Q3 adjusted gross margin was a one-time tariff refund, and scarcity-driven pricing gains reverse if capacity catches up in FY2028
New Canadian tariff regime estimated at ~$10M per quarter
Competition from Nokia/Infinera, Cisco/Acacia, Marvell and Broadcom, plus hyperscaler in-sourcing of optical designs
Economic dilution above the warrant strike from the $2.875B convertible note issue if the shares move sharply higher
Stock trades below both its 50-day ($376.26) and 200-day ($388.43) moving averages with a 52-week range of $143.19-$637.51 — realised volatility is extreme
